reason: The provided sources contain over 15 multi-site verified claims detailing Uranus's discovery, unique axial tilt, 42-year seasons, atmospheric composition, and Voyager 2 flyby.
story: In 1781, astronomer William Herschel discovered Uranus, initially mistaking it for a comet. He tried naming it after King George III, but astronomers eventually named it Uranus, making it the only planet named after a Greek god. Orbiting 2 billion miles from Earth, Uranus turned out to be an ice giant knocked completely on its side. Because of its extreme tilt and 84-Earth-year orbit around the Sun, Uranus experiences 42-year seasons of nonstop daylight followed by 42 years of continuous darkness. Methane in its atmosphere gives the planet its aquamarine color, and despite being an ice giant, it is the coldest planet in the Solar System. In January 1986, NASA's Voyager 2 made the first and only flyby of Uranus, skimming within 50,600 miles of its cloud tops. Decades later, planetary scientists have designated a return flagship probe mission to Uranus as a top priority.
angle: Uranus orbits the Sun knocked completely on its side, creating 42-year-long seasons of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of pitch darkness.

claims.claim: Herschel initially mistook Uranus for a comet when he observed it.
Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun.
Uranus is categorized as an ice giant planet.
NASA's Voyager 2 flew by Uranus in 1986.
Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus.
Uranus takes 84 Earth years to complete one orbit around the Sun.
Uranus orbits the Sun knocked sideways on its rotational axis.
Uranus's extreme axial tilt causes each pole to experience 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of continuous darkness.
Uranus is the coldest planet in the Solar System.
Methane in Uranus's atmosphere gives the planet its cyan/blue appearance.
Herschel originally tried to name Uranus after King George III.
Uranus is the only planet whose English name derives from Greek mythology rather than Roman.
Voyager 2 passed within 50,600 miles of Uranus's cloud tops during its flyby.
The Uranian moon Miranda was discovered in 1948.
Sending a flagship probe mission to Uranus was recommended as a top priority in a Planetary Science Decadal Survey.

disputed: The exact cause of Uranus's sideways tilt and missing internal heat is unproven; scientists speculate a massive protoplanet impact knocked it over and released its heat, which a script should attribute: 'according to one leading theory'.

Whether the highly asymmetrical magnetic field observed by Voyager 2 is Uranus's normal state or an anomaly caused by high solar wind during the flyby is disputed; attribute: 'according to recent re-analysis'.
